source_requirement: Exact independently reviewed pushed feature/integration commit; root issues the source and attempt binding after review.

runtime.capture_requirement: Exact source including shared namespace, private interpreter/framework, stdlib, 54-package combined inventory, static native dependency graph, startup files, OS build and selected-wheel archive provenance; original 50 lock remains unchanged; no self-issued promotion.

model.snapshot_requirement: Revalidate the already reviewed complete private model/tokenizer snapshots and retained inventories; no download or conversion authorized.

input_review.semantics: Final assistant target only; all earlier turns remain ordered masked context; enable_thinking=false. All rows fit intact.
input_review.coverage: Batch2 x 50updates = exactly one seeded permutation of100trainingrows; all20validationrows evaluated each validation pass and saved-final-adapter reload.
checks: Exact source commitments and split/group eligibility
Every selected row tokenized intact without truncation, dropping or resplitting
Shared native exact-ID/label and batch contract; actual per-split padded tokens retained

acceptance: Fresh independent final-source/runtime/profile/admission review, one original single-use start only
Exactly50completed optimizer updates,100unique training row IDs visited in first pass, no row/tail loss
All20heldoutrows included in every native validation traversal and separately reloaded saved-final-adapter validation
Finite nonzero saved-adapter delta, exact native artifact verification and public role readback
300second worker wall deadline plus5second termination grace; a timeout is retained failure, never replay authority
A completed pass and held-out loss are workflow evidence, not a conversational or current Nexus API quality claim
time_feasibility: No measured representative-data throughput exists. Review actual padded tokens and memory; worker stays bounded300seconds even if completion is infeasible. At batch2,50updates visit the full100rows; lowering updates would reduce coverage and is not a one-pass success.
